name: windows-gui-test-vm-gcp
description: Working recipe for testing the OrcaSlicer/JusPrin GUI headlessly on a GPU-less Windows VM in GCP, and the four traps that make it fail silently.
metadata:
  type: project
---

A Windows GUI test VM for this app works in GCP with no GPU. Instance
`jusprin-win-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-central1-a`,
n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB, Cascade Lake), 500 GB pd-balanced,
Windows Server 2022. Harness + full README live outside the repo
at `/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/`. Verified 2026-09-07 end to end:
launch, screenshot, scripted click, verify the UI advanced.

**Why:** four failure modes here are silent — they look like "the app has no
window" or "the app hung" rather than reporting an error, so they cost hours if
rediscovered from scratch.

**How to apply:**
- OpenGL: the app hard-requires 3.2 and Windows software rendering is 1.1. Drop
  Mesa's `opengl32.dll` + `libgallium_wgl.dll` beside the .exe. Then force
  `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` — otherwise Mesa picks
  its d3d12 backend (the GCE virtual display exposes a D3D12 device) and crashes
  on the first frame.
- Never copy the whole Mesa .7z to the VM: Defender deletes it as
  Trojan:Win32/Suschil!rfn. Extract the two DLLs elsewhere, copy only those, and
  no AV exclusion is needed.
- Session isolation is the big one: display APIs, EnumWindows and
  MainWindowTitle only see the calling session's window station, so over SSH they
  report nothing and it reads as "no window exists". Run anything UI-touching as a
  scheduled task with `-LogonType Interactive`.
- Auto-logon must be re-applied on every boot; the GCE image clears the Winlogon
  values after the boot that sets them.
- Resolution needs `gcloud compute instances update --enable-display-device`
  (instance must be stopped) or you get 640x480, smaller than the app's own window.
- WebView2 runtime is absent on a clean Windows Server image; without it the app
  blocks on a modal prompt at startup. Matters especially for JusPrin's
  WebView-based UI. See [[jusprin-rebrand-seams]].

Claude Code and the Claude desktop app are both installed for `guitest`
(2026-09-08). CLI: the native Windows installer `irm https://claude.ai/install.ps1`
puts `claude.exe` in `C:\Users\guitest\.local\bin` - no Node needed, the box has
none. Desktop app: install with Anthropic's own Intune script,
`https://downloads.claude.ai/releases/enterprise/intune/Install-Claude.ps1 -Scope User`,
which resolves the official MSIX and verifies its signature and publisher identity.
MSIX deployment works on this Windows Server 2022 image. Launch the packaged app in
session 1 through explorer.exe, so it lands at normal integrity even though the
scheduled task is elevated:
`Invoke-InSession -Exe C:\Windows\explorer.exe -ArgLine "shell:AppsFolder\Claude_pzs8sxrjxfjjc!Claude"`.
Electron renders fine on this GPU-less VM with no flags.

RDP: port 3389 is open project-wide via `default-allow-rdp` (to 0.0.0.0/0 - not
narrowed yet), and RDP as `guitest` reconnects to the existing console session
rather than starting a second one. Run `./get-rdp-password.sh` in the harness to
print the current credentials; it resolves the ephemeral IP itself and verifies
the password actually authenticates before handing it to you. Do NOT use
`gcloud compute reset-windows-password` - autologon.ps1 re-syncs the account to
Winlogon\DefaultPassword at the next boot and would undo it.

autologon.ps1 used to mint a NEW random password on every boot, so any reboot
silently invalidated the RDP credentials. Fixed 2026-09-09: it now reuses the
stored DefaultPassword and only generates one when that value is absent (delete
the value and reboot to rotate deliberately). This matters because Windows
Update on this VM is set to install and restart on its own, daily at 3 AM, and
the box has also rebooted unexpectedly several times - Kernel-Power event 41,
cause not established.

Two mechanical traps: nested quoting through `winssh.sh` into `powershell -Command`
mangles almost anything non-trivial - write a .ps1, scp it, run it with `-File`.
And a PATH change made over SSH does not reach session 1's already-running Explorer;
re-set the variable from inside the session and restart Explorer, or a new terminal
there still will not find the command.

Tuned 2026-09-08, both changes measured. Windows Defender had real-time scanning
on with zero exclusions, so it scanned every object file the compiler wrote.
Excluding C:\src, C:\tools, C:\guitest plus the compiler binaries took a
small-file write benchmark from 545 to 983 files/s and reads from 979 to 2257 -
roughly 1.8x and 2.3x, for free. Re-add these if the VM is ever rebuilt.

The boot disk was grown 100 -> 500 GB. On GCE a balanced persistent disk's speed
scales with its provisioned size (140 MB/s + 0.28 per GB), so the old 100 GB disk
was capped at 168 MB/s - it was slow *because* it was small. Aggregate write went
from that 168 ceiling to a measured 262 MB/s. Resize is online: `gcloud compute
disks resize`, then `Resize-Partition` on disk 0 partition 3; C: is the last
partition so nothing blocks the extend, and no reboot is needed.

**Do not benchmark GCE persistent disk with one synchronous writer.** A single
WriteThrough stream is latency-bound and reported only 185 MB/s on the 500 GB
disk, which reads as 'the resize did nothing'. Eight concurrent writers showed the
real 262 MB/s. Use concurrent writers - that is also what a parallel build does.

RDP now prefers the H.264 codec: AVC444ModePreferred=1 (DWORD) under
HKLM\SOFTWARE\Policies\Microsoft\Windows NT\Terminal Services, effective on the
next connection. That does not touch the real interactivity limit, which is the
~57 ms round-trip from California to us-central1; only moving the VM to a west
coast region fixes that.

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on every stop/start.

name: windows-build-on-gcp-vm
description: JusPrin builds and runs on the GCP Windows VM; the five traps that make it fail, and why the CI Windows job failing is a runner-environment problem, not a script bug.
metadata:
  type: project
---

JusPrin compiles from source on the Windows test VM and the built binary runs
with its Agent UI visible. Verified 2026-09-07 on n2-standard-16: deps 22.7 min,
slicer 23.0 min. Output is `orca-slicer.exe` (261 KB launcher) plus
`OrcaSlicer.dll` (122.7 MB). Full recipe in
`/Users/kenneth/jusprin-win-vm-harness/BUILDING.md`; VM setup in its README.
See [[windows-gui-test-vm-gcp]].

**Why:** four of the five failures below produce misleading errors far from
their cause, and two were self-inflicted by how the build was driven.

**How to apply:**
- Run long builds as a Windows **scheduled task** (SYSTEM / ServiceAccount), not
  over SSH — OpenSSH kills the process tree on disconnect. Never let two builds
  share a directory: that produced OpenSSL `C1033 cannot open program database`.
- Add `C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin` to PATH so **awk** is found, or libpng
  cannot generate `pngprefix.h` (`-DPNG_PREFIX=` in deps/PNG/PNG.cmake) and you
  get a confusing `C1083` on a header that was never written.
- Set `CMAKE_POLICY_VERSION_MINIMUM=3.5` for CMake 4.x.
- **Do not use the CI deps artifact** — the shipped bundle predates `deps/Eigen`
  and cannot satisfy Eigen 5.0.1. Build deps from source.
- Never hard-stop the VM mid-build: doing so left 622 installed files full of
  NUL bytes and surfaced as fake syntax errors inside Boost headers.
- Qhull is deliberately excluded on MSVC (deps/CMakeLists.txt), so 24/25 is
  complete on Windows.
- To run headless, use the app's own hook rather than dropping DLLs beside the
  exe: `src/OrcaSlicer_app_msvc.cpp` loads `<exedir>\mesa\opengl32.dll` when
  system OpenGL < 2.0. Still force `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe`.

The `Build all` Windows CI job fails at `cmake -G "Visual Studio 17 2022"` with
"could not find any instance of Visual Studio". That is a GitHub runner
environment problem, not `build_release_vs.bat` — the same script selects the
same generator on the VM and configures fine against registered Build Tools.

**MSVC rejects `this` in a nested lambda's init-capture.** Found 2026-09-07 at
commit fbe5963b: `CallAfter([self=wxWeakRef<wxWindow>(this),...])` written INSIDE
another lambda compiled on clang but failed on MSVC with 37 errors, because MSVC
bound that `this` to the enclosing closure object, so it tried to build a
`wxWeakRef<wxWindow>` from a lambda pointer
(`Tracked_class_should_inherit_from_wxTrackable`). Name the object first —
`auto* menu = this;` then capture `menu`. Watch for this pattern whenever a
deferred callback is set up from within another lambda; it is invisible on macOS.

**PowerShell splits `-m:6` (2026-10-24).** In a .ps1, `& cmake --build … -- -m:6 -v:m`
reaches MSBuild as `-m:` `6` and fails at once ("For switch syntax, type
MSBuild -help"). Quote them: `'-m:6' '-v:m'`. Also `*>>` writes UTF-16, so
Select-String on that log matches nothing; use `2>&1 | Out-File -Encoding utf8`.
A watcher built from `winssh.sh 'powershell -Command "…\"…\"…"'` silently never
matched for 3 hours — the quoting rule above applies to status checks too.
Killing "my" processes by command-line match also took out a taskhostw.exe;
kill the PIDs your own task started (and their /T trees), not a pattern.

**Shell harness on the VM (2026-11-07, app-menus).** `C:\src\JusPrin\build\tests\shell\Release\shell_integration_harness.exe` has Mesa beside it; run it from a .cmd with `GALLIUM_DRIVER=llvmpipe` and `LIBGL_ALWAYS_SOFTWARE=1` through an Interactive scheduled task as guitest; it uses its own temp data dir. Build it with `cmake --build build --config Release --target jusprin_web shell_integration_harness -- '-m:12'` (node is at `C:\Users\guitest\.local\node-v24.21.0-win-x64`). The VM has no access to unpushed commits: send them with `git bundle create f.bundle <branch> ^<vm-head>`.
- MSVC also rejects a local `constexpr` used inside a lambda that doesn't capture it (C3493; clang accepts). Make it `static constexpr`.
- On jusprin-newui b0a2fe3b08 the default suite already fails 6 checks on Windows: three failed_autosave_* checks (the harness simulates a failed save by removing write permission, and Windows ignores that on folders), earlier_model_version_available, and agent_panel_columns_tile_the_client at 1000 and 1400 DIP. Compare against that list before blaming a change.
- In PowerShell, `[IO.File]` takes relative paths from the process folder, not from Set-Location; use absolute paths. In a .cmd, `echo exit=%ERRORLEVEL%>> f` turns `0>>` into a redirect; put a space before `>>`.

name: linux-arm-docker-build
description: JusPrin/OrcaSlicer deps build cleanly on ARM Linux in Docker on the Mac; recipe, gotchas, and the GUI-testing path.
metadata:
  type: project
---

All 25 OrcaSlicer dependencies compile on aarch64 Linux — verified 2026-09-07,
45 minutes wall clock, exit 0, artifacts confirmed `ELF 64-bit ARM aarch64`.
No arch-specific patches were needed.

**Do not write a new Dockerfile.** `build_linux.sh -g` already embeds one
(function `docker_runner_dockerfile`, Ubuntu 24.04, and it already branches on
`aarch64|arm64` for the CMake download). Extract it or use `-g` directly.

Recipe that worked:
- Image: `orca-linux-builder:arm64`, built from that embedded Dockerfile with a
  minimal context (only `build_linux.sh` + `scripts/linux.d` are COPYed).
- Workspace: Docker **named volume** `orca-work`, populated with
  `git archive HEAD | docker run -i -v orca-work:/work ... tar -x`.
  Never bind-mount the repo: `build_linux.sh` does `sed --in-place` on
  `version.inc` and writes Linux artifacts into `deps/build/` next to the
  macOS `deps/build/arm64`. VirtioFS bind mounts are also slow for builds.
- Run: `./build_linux.sh -dr -j 6` with `--memory=10g` so the build cannot
  starve the ~18 other containers on this machine.

Gotchas hit, in order:
1. `github.com/.../archive/refs/tags/*.zip` returns **504** intermittently and
   CMake caches the zero-byte result. The Mac host got the same 504, so it is
   GitHub, not the container. Fix: fetch from `codeload.github.com/<org>/<repo>/zip/refs/tags/<tag>`
   and drop it into `deps/DL_CACHE/<Dep>/<file>`; the hash check then passes.
2. `cc1plus` OOM-killed during OpenVDB. Docker Desktop was set to **4 GB**
   while OrcaSlicer's own script demands 10 GB. Raised to 16 GB (settings-store.json
   and settings.json, keys `MemoryMiB`/`memoryMiB`, then restart Docker Desktop).
3. After a Docker Desktop restart, 8 of 18 containers have restart policy `no`
   (the whole `prind-*` Klipper stack, `tsd-enterprise-db-1` Postgres,
   `tsd-enterprise-object_store-1`) and must be `docker start`ed by hand.
   Snapshot `docker ps` before restarting Docker.
4. `| tee` masks the build exit code — use `set -o pipefail`.

GUI testing on top of this: Xvfb + Mesa `llvmpipe` gives **OpenGL 4.5** inside
the container, enough for the 3D plater canvas. Capture with ImageMagick
`import -window root` into a shared dir and read the PNG. `xdotool` for input.
Software rendering, so it is not a faithful check of GPU-specific behavior.
See [[live-test-built-app-on-mac]] for the native macOS path.

name: jusprin-worktree-build
description: How to configure a JusPrin worktree build reusing existing deps; BUILD_TESTS=ON needed for tests
metadata: 
  node_type: memory
  type: reference
  originSessionId: 01c34c35-1546-40fb-a600-c49b2e1ffa06
  modified: 2026-09-18T23:36:14.653Z
---

A JusPrin git worktree builds against the already-built deps by configuring:

```
cmake -B build/arm64 -G "Ninja Multi-Config" -DCMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
  -DCMAKE_OSX_ARCHITECTURES=arm64 -DCMAKE_OSX_DEPLOYMENT_TARGET=15.0 \
  -DCMAKE_PREFIX_PATH="/Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local;/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/OrcaSlicer_dep/usr/local" \
  -DSLIC3R_GUI=ON -DSLIC3R_STATIC=ON -DSLIC3R_PCH=ON -DBUILD_TESTS=ON \
  -DCMAKE_AR=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ar -DCMAKE_RANLIB=/opt/homebrew/opt/llvm/bin/llvm-ranlib
```

CMAKE BINARY (2026-09-29): configure with `/Applications/CMake.app/Contents/bin/cmake` (put it first on PATH). Homebrew's cmake 4.1 at /opt/homebrew/bin fails with "Could NOT find Eigen3 (missing: EIGEN3_VERSION_OK) (Required is at least version 5.0.1)", and a failed configure poisons the cache: `rm -rf build` before retrying.

The two `CMAKE_AR`/`CMAKE_RANLIB` flags are required on a FRESH build dir:
without them Apple's ar is used and liblibslic3r_gui.a (>4 GiB in
RelWithDebInfo) fails to archive. They only work at first configure, not on
reconfigure. Full story: agent-docs/macos-build-troubleshooting.md. See
[[liblibslic3r-gui-4gib-ar-limit]].

FRESH WORKTREE TRAP (2026-09-18): building only `shell_integration_harness`
does not build the web pages. Also build `--target jusprin_web jusprin_catalogs`
(needs node on PATH: /Users/kenneth/.nvm/versions/node/v24.13.0/bin). Without
them resources/jusprin/{home,agent}/index.html are missing, no web views are
created, and the harness silently tests something else (printer panel starts
shown; web-view crashes vanish).

`BUILD_TESTS=ON` is required or the tests/ tree (workspace, shell targets) is
not generated. Build with `cmake --build build/arm64 --config RelWithDebInfo
--target <targets>`. wxWidgets 3.3 sources for API verification live under
/Users/kenneth/Projects/OrcaSlicer/deps/build/arm64/dep_wxWidgets-prefix/.

CWD TRAP (cost real time once): the harness resets the Bash cwd to the main
repo /Users/kenneth/Projects/JusPrin between turns, so a *relative*
`cmake --build build/arm64` silently builds the MAIN repo's build dir, not the
worktree's — the worktree binary then runs stale code and a re-fix looks like it
"didn't take". Always pass the worktree build dir as an ABSOLUTE path to
`cmake --build /…/.claude/worktrees/<wt>/build/arm64 …`, and run test binaries by
absolute path. Also: `cmake --build --target <one_exe>` may relink against a
stale lib without recompiling a changed .cpp in that lib — build the app target
(e.g. OrcaSlicer) too so the lib recompiles; verify with
`grep -c '<file>.cpp.o' build.log`. Editing tools (Edit/Write) use absolute
paths so source edits land correctly regardless of cwd.

STALE PROMPT TRAP (2026-09-23): `--target shell_integration_harness` does NOT
rebuild the web pages, so a harness run after an edit to AgentUI (for example
printerInstructions.ts) loads the old bundle. Six --printer-live runs were
wasted this way. After any page edit, build `jusprin_web` explicitly and check
the new text is in resources/jusprin/agent/index.html before running live.

DISK (2026-10-10): building with `--config Release` instead of RelWithDebInfo made a fresh worktree build dir 859 MB instead of ~14 GB, needed no llvm-ar relink, and the shell harness ran normally from `tests/shell/Release/`. Use it when the disk is nearly full (it was at 99%) and no debugger is needed. With other sessions building, a fresh build took far longer than usual (machine load 30 to 85).

# single-config generators (CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE set) and multi-config generators
# (Ninja Multi-Config, Visual Studio) where CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE is empty and DLLs
# must land in every per-config output directory. On Windows the loader finds
# DLLs in the executable's directory; the Linux branch below does the same for
# the deps-built FFmpeg libraries and adds an $ORIGIN rpath, since the ELF
# loader does not search the executable's directory and the CI unit-test runner
# only receives the tests artifact (no deps install).
function(orcaslicer_copy_test_dlls)
    if (WIN32)
        set(_configs ${CMAKE_CONFIGURATION_TYPES})
        if (NOT _configs)
            set(_configs "${CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE}")
        endif()
        foreach(_cfg IN LISTS _configs)
            if (_cfg STREQUAL "Debug")

# JusPrin Linux GUI test VM

A GCP VM for building JusPrin on Linux and testing its GUI, either by hand over
remote desktop or by script on a headless display.

| | |
|---|---|
| Instance | `jusprin-linux-test`, project `elegoo-backend`, zone `us-west2-a` (Los Angeles, for low latency from California) |
| Machine | n2-standard-16 (16 vCPU, 64 GB), 300 GB pd-balanced, no GPU |
| OS | Ubuntu 24.04 LTS, XFCE desktop |
| Toolchain | Ubuntu's gcc 13, CMake 4.3.0 (same as the CI runner, in /opt), Node 24.11.1 (in /opt) |
| Checkout | `~/JusPrin` on branch `jusprin-dev` (user `kenneth`) |
| OpenGL | Mesa llvmpipe, OpenGL 4.5 core, software rendering |

The VM has no service account, so it cannot call GCP APIs. It cannot fetch the
private GitHub repo either; send commits with a git bundle (below).

## Scripts (run on the Mac)

- `./vmssh.sh '<command>'` runs a command on the VM.
- `./vmscp.sh <src> <dst>` copies files; write `VM:~/path` for the VM side.
- `./connect-rdp.sh` starts the VM if stopped, prints the login, and holds an SSH
  tunnel open. Point Windows App (Microsoft Remote Desktop) at `localhost:33890`,
  user `kenneth`. xrdp listens only on the VM's own localhost, so the project-wide
  `default-allow-rdp` firewall rule does not expose it.
- `env.sh` holds the instance name and forces the `ai-agent` service account. It
  also points gcloud at uv's standalone Python 3.12, because Homebrew's Python lost
  its OpenSSL library when Homebrew moved from openssl@3 to openssl@4.

## Scripts (copied to the VM's home folder)

- `~/vm-run-app.sh [args]` starts the built app on headless display `:99` (Xvfb
  with the xfwm4 window manager) with data dir `~/jusprin-test-data`. Log:
  `~/app.log`. It sets `SSL_CERT_FILE`; without it OrcaSlicer's Linux build stops
  at startup on a dialog asking which certificate file to use.
- `~/vm-screenshot.sh` saves display `:99` to `~/shot.png`.
- Click with `DISPLAY=:99 xdotool mousemove X Y click 1`. Screenshot pixels equal
  screen coordinates (1920x1080).
- Stop the app with `pkill -x orca-slicer`. Never `pkill -f orca-slicer` over
  ssh: it matches the ssh command's own text and kills the session.

## Build

```bash
# First time on a fresh VM: deps (about 25 min) then app and tests (about 30 min)
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -dst -j 16
# After code changes: app and tests only
cd ~/JusPrin && ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16
```

The app lands in `~/JusPrin/build/package/bin/orca-slicer`. Run long builds
detached so an ssh disconnect does not kill them:

```bash
setsid nohup bash -c 'set -o pipefail; ./build_linux.sh -st -j 16 2>&1 | tee ~/build.log; echo BUILD_EXIT=$? >> ~/build.log' >/dev/null 2>&1 </dev/null &
```

Tests: `cd ~/JusPrin/build && DISPLAY=:99 ctest -C Release -j 8`.

## Sending new commits

```bash
git bundle create f.bundle jusprin-dev ^<commit the VM already has>
./vmscp.sh f.bundle VM:~/
./vmssh.sh 'cd ~/JusPrin && git pull ~/f.bundle jusprin-dev'
```

## Cost

The VM bills while running. Stop it when idle:

```bash
gcloud compute instances stop jusprin-linux-test --project elegoo-backend --zone us-west2-a
```

The external IP is ephemeral and changes on each start; the scripts look it up
by name, so nothing needs editing.

- `ai-agent` cannot attach the default compute service account; create VMs with

  stores `refs/remotes/origin/jusprin-dev`, so `git clone -b jusprin-dev` fails;
  fetch that ref explicitly.
- Set `SSL_CERT_FILE=/etc/ssl/certs/ca-certificates.crt` or the app blocks at
  startup on a certificate-store dialog.
- `pkill -f orca-slicer` over ssh kills the ssh session itself; use `pkill -x`.
- Homebrew moved openssl@3 to @4 on 2026-11-09 and broke gcloud's Python;
  env.sh sets CLOUDSDK_PYTHON to uv's standalone CPython 3.12.
- jusprin-dev 41f8843929 does not configure on Linux with tests on: the 2.5.0

  and applied uncommitted on the VM checkout.

5:JusPrin is a long-lived fork. Every line it changes in an OrcaSlicer-owned file is a line it re-resolves at every rebase, forever, by a person who was not there when the line was written. The rules below exist to keep that permanent cost small and, where it cannot be small, to keep it visible.
79:**Rule.** When you must delete or relocate an upstream line, say at the site what moved, where it went, and what a future rebase must carry across.
99:**Rule.** Before asserting that a change is or is not rebase-risky, check it. Three checks, each one command: does git actually conflict there; has upstream already converged on the same change; is the change a move or a duplication.
105:**Violation.** A report that lists which files are rebase-sensitive and calls the change narrow, without having run the merge simulation that would have found two lossy resolutions waiting in it.
111:**Mechanism.** The fork follows upstream's release branches, and each release branch splits off upstream's development line on its own. A plain merge picks the common ancestor itself, a development-line commit from before both release branches. Its conflict list is then everything that differs between the two release branches: vendor profiles, translations, CI files, none of it ours. Naming the last release we took as the base limits the merge to the fork's own changes. That gives the same conflicts a replay would hit, resolved once, with no commits rewritten, so branches in progress merge forward without a rebase. Measured on 2026-11-07, going from v2.4.2 to v2.5.0: 22 conflicted files either way, and a branch in progress merged into the trial result with no conflicts.
130:1. **The rebase simulation and its result.** Run it against the newest upstream release, with the release the fork last took as the base (rule 10), and name both endpoint commits — measurements are not reproducible otherwise.
142:An automatic merge is evidence about today's text. It is not proof that a future rebase will merge, and never proof that the merged result behaves correctly. After every upstream update, run the focused contract tests, the full native build, the real multi-plate workflow, native gizmo input, and the stock-behavior regression checks.
